sections.text: The cystic artery usually crosses posterior to the common bile duct within the hepatobiliary triangle and follows the cystic duct along its superior surface to the neck of the gallbladder. Its relationship to the biliary ducts is variable (Andall et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2000).

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: Typically, upon reaching the superior aspect of the neck of the gallbladder, the cystic artery bifurcates. A superficial branch passes deep to the visceral peritoneum along the gallbladder’s inferior surface. A deep branch runs between the superior surface of the gallbladder and the substance of the liver that is its fossa.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The cystic artery supplies the gallbladder. It also contributes branches that anastomose with the main arteries supplying the cystic duct, common hepatic duct, and common bile duct.

sections.title: References
sections.text:
Andall, R. G., Matusz, P., du Plessis, M., Ward, R., Tubbs, R. S. and Loukas, M. (2016) 'The clinical anatomy of cystic artery variations: a review of over 9800 cases', Surg Radiol Anat, 38(5), pp. 529-39.

Chen, T. H., Shyu, J. F., Chen, C. H., Ma, K. H., Wu, C. W., Lui, W. Y. and Liu, J. C. (2000) 'Variations of the cystic artery in Chinese adults', Surg Laparosc Endosc Percutan Tech, 10(3), pp. 154-7.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Superior mesenteric artery.

Course: Passes to the right on the posterior surface of the portal vein.

Branches: Terminates as part of a network of anastomotic branches around the distal end of the common bile duct.

Supplied Structures: The portion of the common bile duct posterior to the duodenum and within the parenchyma of the pancreas.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The retroportal artery arises from the superior mesenteric artery, or, potentially, from the celiac trunk (Northover and Terblanche, 1979).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: Regardless of origin, the retroportal artery passes to the right on the posterior surface of the portal vein.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The retroportal artery terminates as part of a network of anastomotic branches around the distal end of the common bile duct.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The retroportal artery supplies the distal portion of the common bile duct that includes the segment posterior to first part of the duodenum. It then passes into the parenchyma of the pancreas.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Northover, J. M. and Terblanche, J. (1979) 'A new look at the arterial supply of the bile duct in man and its surgical implications', Br J Surg, 66(6), pp. 379-84.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: The extrahepatic bile ducts are supplied by several sources. The common bile duct and the hepatic ducts receive arterial blood from the right hepatic artery, which is reinforced by the cystic artery. The distal end of the bile duct supplied by the posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal, retroduodenal, and retroportal arteries.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Left hepatic artery.

Course: Passes to the right as far as the umbilical fissure.

Branches: Continues as Segment IV Artery.

Supplied Structures: Liver segment IV.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text:
The medial segmental artery arises from the left hepatic artery, though this is quite variable.

There is great confusion in the parameters of the medial segmental artery of the liver. In many cases, it is synonymous with segmental IV artery, and even its presence is often called into question as Segmental IV artery is commonly observed as a branch of the right hepatic artery (Jin et al., 2008; Favelier et al., 2015).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The medial segmental artery emerges from the left hepatic artery shortly after it enters the liver parenchyma and passes to the right as far as the umbilical fissure.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The medial segmental artery continues as Segment IV Artery, a macroscopic end artery.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The medial segmental artery supplies liver segment IV, both superiorly (segment IVa) and inferiorly (segment IVb).

sections.title: References
sections.text:
Favelier, S., Germain, T., Genson, P. Y., Cercueil, J. P., Denys, A., Krausé, D. and Guiu, B. (2015) 'Anatomy of liver arteries for interventional radiology', Diagn Interv Imaging, 96(6), pp. 537-46.

Jin, G. Y., Yu, H. C., Lim, H. S., Moon, J. I., Lee, J. H., Chung, J. W. and Cho, B. H. (2008) 'Anatomical variations of the origin of the segment 4 hepatic artery and their clinical implications', Liver Transpl, 14(8), pp. 1180-4.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The segment VII artery arises from the posterior segmental artery of liver.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The segment VII artery usually emerges as a tangle of small branches that pass superiorly.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The segment VII artery supplies segment VII of the liver.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Left hepatic artery.

Course: Passes superiorly and to the left, arches over the left branch of the portal vein.

Branches: Bifurcates into two segmental arteries; segmental II and III arteries.

Supplied Structures: Liver segments II and III.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The lateral segmental artery arises from the left hepatic artery after it arches over the portal vein.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The lateral segmental artery passes superiorly and to the left. It arches over the posterior (umbilical) portion of the left branch of the portal vein.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The lateral segmental artery bifurcates into two segmental arteries, segmental II artery (A2) and segmental III artery (A3).

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The lateral segmental artery supplies segments II and III of the liver.

16607.name: Anterior Segmental Artery of Liver
alternate: Anterior Sectoral Branch of Right Hepatic Branch

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Right hepatic artery.

Course: Passes straight superiorly and to the right.

Branches: Segmental branch V and VIII.

Supplied Structures: Caudate lobe (Segment 1), Segments V and VIII of the liver.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The anterior segmental artery of the liver arises from the right hepatic artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: Typically, the right hepatic artery within the parenchyma of the right functional lobe of the liver quickly gives a side branch, then bifurcates into two terminal branches, one of which is the anterior segmental artery of the liver. It passes relatively straight, superior and to the right (Furuta et al., 2009).

sections.title: Branches
sections.text:
The anterior segmental artery gives several segmental branches variably to Segment 1 (caudate lobe) and provides terminal branches to Segments V and VIII (Favelier et al., 2015).

Note that from the common hepatic artery to the terminal branches, the vasculature of the hepatobiliary system is extremely variable. What is given here is the most common arrangement. However, any surgeon operating in this area must first establish the branching pattern either radiographically or by exploration before ligating any vessel in this region.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The anterior segmental artery provides arterial supply to segment I (caudate lobe), segment V, and segment VIII of the liver (Favelier et al., 2015).

sections.title: References
sections.text:
Favelier, S., Germain, T., Genson, P. Y., Cercueil, J. P., Denys, A., Krausé, D. and Guiu, B. (2015) 'Anatomy of liver arteries for interventional radiology', Diagn Interv Imaging, 96(6), pp. 537-46.

Furuta, T., Maeda, E., Akai, H., Hanaoka, S., Yoshioka, N., Akahane, M., Watadani, T. and Ohtomo, K. (2009) 'Hepatic Segments and Vasculature: Projecting CT Anatomy onto Angiograms', Radiographics, 29(7), pp. e37.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The segment VIII artery arises from the anterior segmental artery of liver.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The segment VIII artery courses superiorly until it bifurcates.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The segment VIII artery provides a branch, A8 ventral, inferior to the superior surface of the liver, and a branch, A8 dorsal, terminating at the very superior surface of the liver, just inferior to the diaphragm (Furuta et al., 2009).

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The segment VIII artery supplies segment VIII of the liver.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Furuta, T., Maeda, E., Akai, H., Hanaoka, S., Yoshioka, N., Akahane, M., Watadani, T. and Ohtomo, K. (2009) 'Hepatic Segments and Vasculature: Projecting CT Anatomy onto Angiograms', Radiographics, 29(7), pp. e37.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The segment V artery arises from the anterior segmental artery of the liver.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The segment V artery courses posteriorly, inferiorly, and to the right (Furuta et al., 2009).

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: Typically, the segment V artery does not give rise to a single vessel, but rather a group of small vessels (Furuta et al., 2009).

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The segment V artery supplies segment V of the liver.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Furuta, T., Maeda, E., Akai, H., Hanaoka, S., Yoshioka, N., Akahane, M., Watadani, T. and Ohtomo, K. (2009) 'Hepatic Segments and Vasculature: Projecting CT Anatomy onto Angiograms', Radiographics, 29(7), pp. e37.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The segment VI artery arises from the posterior segmental artery of liver.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The segment VI artery courses inferior and to the right to the lower, right corner of the liver. Often, it is the longest and most prominent of the posterior running branches (Furuta et al., 2009).

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The segment VI artery supplies segment VI of the liver.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Furuta, T., Maeda, E., Akai, H., Hanaoka, S., Yoshioka, N., Akahane, M., Watadani, T. and Ohtomo, K. (2009) 'Hepatic Segments and Vasculature: Projecting CT Anatomy onto Angiograms', Radiographics, 29(7), pp. e37.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text:
The segment IV artery may be viewed as the distal continuation of the medial segmental artery of liver.

There is great confusion in the parameters of the segment IV artery of the liver. In many cases, it is synonymous with medial segmental artery. Segment IV artery is commonly observed to be a branch of the right hepatic artery (Jin et al., 2008; Favelier et al., 2015).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: This intrahepatic branch passes to the right as far as the umbilical fissure.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The segment IV artery supplies segment IV of the liver, often called the quadrate lobe of the liver.

sections.title: References
sections.text:
Favelier, S., Germain, T., Genson, P. Y., Cercueil, J. P., Denys, A., Krausé, D. and Guiu, B. (2015) 'Anatomy of liver arteries for interventional radiology', Diagn Interv Imaging, 96(6), pp. 537-46.

Jin, G. Y., Yu, H. C., Lim, H. S., Moon, J. I., Lee, J. H., Chung, J. W. and Cho, B. H. (2008) 'Anatomical variations of the origin of the segment 4 hepatic artery and their clinical implications', Liver Transpl, 14(8), pp. 1180-4.

24674.name: Right Hepatic Artery
alternate: Right Branch of Hepatic Artery Proper
Right Branch of Proper Hepatic Artery

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Proper hepatic artery.

Course: Enters the porta hepatis of the liver.

Branches: Cystic artery, anterior, posterior, segmental (lobar) branches; contributes a right caudate branch to shared vascularization of this lobe.

Supplied Structures: Gallbladder and right “functional” lobe of the liver that is composed of segments I (caudate lobe), V, VI, VII and VIII.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The right hepatic artery arises from the proper hepatic artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text:
The proper hepatic artery travels nearly vertically within the hepatoduodenal ligament. It is related to the common bile duct to its right and the portal vein posteriorly. At a variable position along its course, it branches into right and left hepatic arteries. Most often the bifurcation occurs just inferior to the liver where the right hepatic artery would angle off to the right, usually crossing posterior to the common bile duct to enter the liver parenchyma.

Anatomical variation in the disposition of the arteries to the liver occurs in about one third of individuals (Covey et al., 2002; Saba and Mallarini, 2011). The right hepatic artery usually crosses posterior to and is closely related with the common hepatic duct. This proximity means that it is often involved in biliary duct cancers, and before the left hepatic artery. On the occasion where it crosses anterior to the common hepatic duct, it is vulnerable to injury during biliary duct surgery such as cholecystectomy.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The right hepatic artery usually gives off the cystic artery, though this is quite variable. It also supplies the right “functional” lobar segmental arteries, the end arteries to the liver. It usually has a right caudate lobar branch that shares the vascularization of this lobe with a branch from the left hepatic artery.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The right hepatic artery supplies the gallbladder and right “functional” lobe of the liver, i.e., segments I (caudate lobe), V, VI, VII and VIII.

sections.title: List of Clinical Correlates
sections.text: - Cholecystectomy

sections.title: References
sections.text:
Covey, A. M., Brody, L. A., Maluccio, M. A., Getrajdman, G. I. and Brown, K. T. (2002) 'Variant hepatic arterial anatomy revisited: digital subtraction angiography performed in 600 patients', Radiology, 224(2), pp. 542-7.

Saba, L. and Mallarini, G. (2011) 'Anatomic variations of arterial liver vascularization: an analysis by using MDCTA', Surg Radiol Anat, 33(7), pp. 559-68.

20744.name: Left Hepatic Artery
alternate: Left Branch of Hepatic Artery Proper
Left Branch of Proper Hepatic Artery

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Proper hepatic artery.

Course: Enters the porta hepatis of the liver.

Branches: Left artery of caudate lobe and medial and lateral segmental arteries.

Supplied Structures: Left “functional” lobe of the liver that is composed of segments I (caudate lobe), II, III, and IV.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The left hepatic artery arises from the proper hepatic artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text:
The proper hepatic artery ascends nearly vertically within the hepatoduodenal ligament. It travels as part of the portal triad, to the left of the common bile duct and anterior to the portal vein. At a variable position along its course, it branches into right and left hepatic branches. Most often this bifurcation occurs just inferior to the porta hepatis. After branching the left hepatic artery angles to the left and enters the liver parenchyma. Usually within the liver parenchyma the left hepatic artery arches over the portal vein (arch of the left hepatic artery), a defining feature that helps distinguish it on contrast radiographs.

Anatomical variation in the disposition of the arteries to the liver occurs in about one third of individuals (Covey et al., 2002; Saba and Mallarini, 2011).

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The left hepatic artery usually gives off a left artery of the caudate lobe, thus, forming an anastomosis between the left and right hepatic arteries via the right artery of the caudate lobe. The left hepatic artery also gives rise to medial and lateral segmental arteries.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The left hepatic artery supplies the left “physiological” lobe of the liver composed of segments I (caudate lobe), II, III, and IV. Segment I usually exhibits shared vascularization from the left and right hepatic arteries.

sections.title: References
sections.text:
Covey, A. M., Brody, L. A., Maluccio, M. A., Getrajdman, G. I. and Brown, K. T. (2002) 'Variant hepatic arterial anatomy revisited: digital subtraction angiography performed in 600 patients', Radiology, 224(2), pp. 542-7.

Saba, L. and Mallarini, G. (2011) 'Anatomic variations of arterial liver vascularization: an analysis by using MDCTA', Surg Radiol Anat, 33(7), pp. 559-68.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Common hepatic artery.

Course: Passes superiorly on the right towards the porta hepatis of the liver.

Branches: Right and left hepatic arteries, often the right gastric artery.

Supplied Structures: Liver, gallbladder, pyloric portion of the stomach (potentially).

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The proper hepatic artery is one of the two terminal branches of the common hepatic artery, the other being the gastroduodenal artery

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The proper hepatic artery passes superiorly within the free edge of the hepatoduodenal ligament. Here it is one of the components of the portal triad (taking the anterior, to the left position). If it gives the right gastric branch (the origin of which is quite variable, but is often the proper hepatic artery) it usually emerges from the proximal part of the proper hepatic artery. The artery bifurcates at a variable distance between its origin and the porta hepatis on the inferior surface of the liver. The branch point most commonly occurs along the superior third of this distance just before the branches enter the parenchyma of the liver.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The proper hepatic artery ends in two terminal branches, right and left hepatic arteries. In over 50% of instances, the right gastric also emerges from the proper hepatic artery (Eckmann and Krahn, 1984), and when it does it is usually from the proximal portion, close to the bifurcation of the common hepatic artery.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The proper hepatic artery supplies the liver, gallbladder, and potentially the pyloric portion of the stomach if the right gastric artery emerges distal to the bifurcation of the common hepatic artery.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Eckmann, I. and Krahn, V. (1984) '[Frequency of different sites of origin of the right gastric artery]', Anat Anz, 155(1-5), pp. 65-70.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Right hepatic artery.

Course: Posterior and medially.

Branches: Small unnamed branches.

Supplied Structures: Lateral portion of the caudate lobe of the liver.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The right artery of the caudate lobe typically arises from the right hepatic artery (Furuta et al., 2009; Miyayama et al., 1990).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The right artery of the caudate lobe courses posteriorly and medially.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The right artery of the caudate lobe gives off multiple small unnamed branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text:
The right artery of the caudate lobe mainly supplies the lateral portion of the caudate lobe (Furuta et al., 2009).

Typically, the caudate lobe receives two arteries, one each from the right and left hepatic arteries (53% of cases). In 35% of individuals, this territory is supplied by the right hepatic artery branch only, or in 12% by the left hepatic artery branch (Furuta et al., 2009).

sections.title: References
sections.text:
Furuta, T., Maeda, E., Akai, H., Hanaoka, S., Yoshioka, N., Akahane, M., Watadani, T. and Ohtomo, K. (2009) 'Hepatic Segments and Vasculature: Projecting CT Anatomy onto Angiograms', Radiographics, 29(7), pp. e37.

Miyayama, S., Matsui, O., Kameyama, T., Hirose, J., Konishi, H., Chyotoh, S., Kadoya, M. and Takashima, T. (1990) '[Angiographic anatomy of arterial branches to the caudate lobe of the liver with special reference to its effect on transarterial embolization of hepatocellular carcinoma]', Rinsho Hoshasen, 35(3), pp. 353-9.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The segment II artery arises from the lateral segmental artery of liver.

sections.title: Course
sections.text:
The segment II artery passes straight to the left corner of the liver, superior to the segmental III artery.

The pattern of segmental artery origins and courses is extremely variable. Most of the research is based on contrast proper hepatic artery arteriography (Furuta et al., 2009; Favelier et al., 2015). The account given is the most common but was found in only 27% of cases in a cadaveric study of 100 livers (Garg et al., 2019).

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The segment II artery supplies segment II of the liver.

sections.title: References
sections.text:
Favelier, S., Germain, T., Genson, P. Y., Cercueil, J. P., Denys, A., Krausé, D. and Guiu, B. (2015) 'Anatomy of liver arteries for interventional radiology', Diagn Interv Imaging, 96(6), pp. 537-46.

Furuta, T., Maeda, E., Akai, H., Hanaoka, S., Yoshioka, N., Akahane, M., Watadani, T. and Ohtomo, K. (2009) 'Hepatic Segments and Vasculature: Projecting CT Anatomy onto Angiograms', Radiographics, 29(7), pp. e37.

Garg, S., Sahni, D., Kumar, H., Yadav, T. D., Aggarwal, A. and Gupta, T. (2019) 'The segmental branching of the hepatic arteries in the liver: a cadaveric study', Anat Sci Int, 94(2), pp. 216-223.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Left hepatic artery (typically).

Course: Passes posteriorly

Branches: Small, unnamed branches

Supplied Structures: Medial portion of the caudate lobe of the liver.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The left artery of the caudate lobe typically arises from the left hepatic artery (Furuta et al., 2009; Miyayama et al., 1990).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The left artery of the caudate lobe courses posteriorly.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The left artery of the caudate lobe gives off multiple small unnamed branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text:
The left artery of the caudate lobe mainly supplies the medial portion of the caudate lobe (Furuta et al., 2009).

Typically, the caudate lobe receives two arteries, one each from the right and left hepatic arteries (53% of cases). In 35% of individuals, this territory is supplied by the right hepatic artery branch only, or in 12% by the left hepatic artery branch (Furuta et al., 2009).

sections.title: References
sections.text:
Furuta, T., Maeda, E., Akai, H., Hanaoka, S., Yoshioka, N., Akahane, M., Watadani, T. and Ohtomo, K. (2009) 'Hepatic Segments and Vasculature: Projecting CT Anatomy onto Angiograms', Radiographics, 29(7), pp. e37.

Miyayama, S., Matsui, O., Kameyama, T., Hirose, J., Konishi, H., Chyotoh, S., Kadoya, M. and Takashima, T. (1990) '[Angiographic anatomy of arterial branches to the caudate lobe of the liver with special reference to its effect on transarterial embolization of hepatocellular carcinoma]', Rinsho Hoshasen, 35(3), pp. 353-9.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Right hepatic artery.

Course: Passes inferior and to the right.

Branches: Segment VI and VII arteries.

Supplied Structures: Liver segments VI and VII.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The posterior segmental artery arises from the right hepatic artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The posterior segmental artery passes inferior and to the right. It tends to meander proximally (Furuta et al., 2009).

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The posterior segmental artery gives rise to segment VI and VII arteries.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The posterior segmental artery provides arterial supply to segments VI and VII of the liver.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Furuta, T., Maeda, E., Akai, H., Hanaoka, S., Yoshioka, N., Akahane, M., Watadani, T. and Ohtomo, K. (2009) 'Hepatic Segments and Vasculature: Projecting CT Anatomy onto Angiograms', Radiographics, 29(7), pp. e37.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The segment III artery arises from the lateral segmental artery of liver.

sections.title: Course
sections.text:
The segment III artery passes inferiorly and to the left. This course takes it in the same direction, but inferior to the segment II artery.

The pattern of segmental artery origins and courses is extremely variable. Most of the research is based on contrast proper hepatic artery arteriography (Furuta et al., 2009; Favelier et al., 2015). The account given is the most common but was found in only 27% of cases in a cadaveric study of 100 livers (Garg et al., 2019).

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The segment III artery supplies segment III of the liver.

sections.title: References
sections.text:
Favelier, S., Germain, T., Genson, P. Y., Cercueil, J. P., Denys, A., Krausé, D. and Guiu, B. (2015) 'Anatomy of liver arteries for interventional radiology', Diagn Interv Imaging, 96(6), pp. 537-46.

Furuta, T., Maeda, E., Akai, H., Hanaoka, S., Yoshioka, N., Akahane, M., Watadani, T. and Ohtomo, K. (2009) 'Hepatic Segments and Vasculature: Projecting CT Anatomy onto Angiograms', Radiographics, 29(7), pp. e37.

Garg, S., Sahni, D., Kumar, H., Yadav, T. D., Aggarwal, A. and Gupta, T. (2019) 'The segmental branching of the hepatic arteries in the liver: a cadaveric study', Anat Sci Int, 94(2), pp. 216-223.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Dorsal pancreatic artery.

Course: Posterior aspect and inferior border of pancreas.

Branches: Numerous small, unnamed branches.

Supplied Structures: Body and tail of pancreas.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The inferior pancreatic artery typically arises from the dorsal pancreatic artery (left terminal branch). Occasionally, it may arise from the gastroduodenal or superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries (Covantev, Mazuruc and Belic, 2019).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The inferior pancreatic artery passes on the posterior aspect and inferior border of the pancreas towards the left.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The inferior pancreatic artery gives rise to numerous small, unnamed branches that heavily anastomose with small pancreatic branches from the splenic artery (Covantev, Mazuruc and Belic, 2019).

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The inferior pancreatic artery supplies the body and tail of the pancreas.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Covantev, S., Mazuruc, N. and Belic, O. (2019) 'The Arterial Supply of the Distal Part of the Pancreas', Surgery Research and Practice, 2019, pp. 1–7.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Splenic artery.

Course: Passes to the left along the posterior surface of the pancreas.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Left half of the body and tail of the pancreas.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The great pancreatic artery arises from the splenic artery, approximately one half to two thirds of the distance along its course, but is quite variable.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The great pancreatic artery passes to the left along the posterior surface of the pancreas aiming towards its tail. It approximates the course of the pancreatic duct.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The great pancreatic artery supplies the left half of the body and tail of the pancreas.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Splenic artery.

Course: Along the length of the pancreas anastomosing with pancreaticoduodenal artery branches (right) and other splenic artery branches.

Branches: Left and right branches.

Supplied Structures: Pancreas.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The dorsal pancreatic artery arises from the proximal portion of the splenic artery, but is highly variable (Tsutsumi et al., 2014).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The dorsal pancreatic artery courses posterior to splenic vein.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: Gives off numerous branches, but the general pattern is that it splits into right and left branches (Tsutsumi et al., 2014). The right branch (anastomotic branch) passes to the right along the posterior surface or within the parenchyma of the pancreas. It extends to anastomose with branches of the superior and inferior posterior pancreatic arteries. The left branch, considered the terminus of the artery (terminal branch), passes along the inferior surface of the pancreas to the left into its tail anastomosing with the transverse pancreatic artery.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The dorsal pancreatic artery supplies the entire pancreas (uncinate process, head, neck, body, and tail) by contributing to arterial arcades of the pancreas.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Tsutsumi, M., Arakawa, T., Terashima, T., Aizawa, Y., Kageyama, I., Kumaki, K. and Miki, A. (2014) 'Morphological analysis of the branches of the dorsal pancreatic artery and their clinical significance', Clin Anat, 27(4), pp. 645-52.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Splenic artery.

Course: Passes to the left within the parenchyma of the pancreas along the superior border.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Tail of pancreas, hilum of spleen.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The origin of the artery to the tail of the pancreas is variable; however, it usually arises from the splenic artery, and sometimes from the greater pancreatic artery (Macchi et al., 2014).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: A variable number (1–5) of small branches travel posterior to and within the parenchyma, along the superior border of the pancreas. The vessels pass to the left, superior to and roughly paralleling the great pancreatic artery, into the tail of the pancreas and out to the hilum of the spleen. It may anastomose with the great pancreatic artery or the splenic artery and share vascular supply with the spleen (Macchi et al., 2014).

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The artery to the tail of pancreas supplies the tail of pancreas, as well as the hilum of the spleen.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Macchi, V., Porzionato, A., Picardi, E. E., Stecco, C., Morra, A., Bardini, R. and De Caro, R. (2014) 'Clinical anatomy of the caudal pancreatic arteries and their relevance in the surgery of the splenic trauma', Ital J Anat Embryol, 119(2), pp. 141-7.

24330.name: Pancreatic Branches of Posterior Superior Pancreaticoduodenal Artery
24330.latin: Rami pancreatici arteriae pancreaticoduodenalis superioris posterioris

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery.

Course: Pass to the left into the head of the pancreas.

Branches: Unnamed anastomotic branches.

Supplied Structures: Head of pancreas.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery gives rise to several small pancreatic branches.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: These small pancreatic branches pass to the left into the head of the pancreas.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The pancreatic branches of the posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery give off several anastomotic branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: As the name suggests, the pancreatic branches of the posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery supply the head of the pancreas.

22190.name: Pancreatic Branches of Anterior Superior Pancreaticoduodenal Artery
22190.latin: Rami pancreatici arteriae pancreaticoduodenalis superioris anterioris
alternate: Pancreatic Branches of Anterior Superior Supraduodenal Artery

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery.

Course: Travel horizontally, to the left, into the head of the pancreas.

Branches: Small anastomotic branches.

Supplied Structures: Head of the pancreas.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery gives rise to a variable number of small pancreatic branches.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The pancreatic branches leave the anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery and travel roughly horizontally, to the left, into the adjacent parenchyma of the head of the pancreas.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The pancreatic branches of the anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery anastomose with the pancreatic branches from the anterior inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The pancreatic branches of the anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery supply the head of the pancreas.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Splenic artery.

Course: Continue a short distance laterally into the hilum of the spleen and enters its parenchyma.

Branches: 4–5 segmental branches.

Supplied Structures: Spleen.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The splenic artery usually gives two branches, one superior and one inferior, before entering the parenchyma of the spleen at the hilum.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The superior and inferior splenic branches pass a short distance left, lateral, into the hilum of the spleen and enter its parenchyma.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: In the spleen parenchyma, the terminal splenic branches of the splenic artery give rise to 4–5 segmental branches. There is little anastomoses between arteries of individual segments such that ligation of a segmental branch leads to ischemia of that portion of the spleen (Pandey et al., 2004; Cortés and Gómez Pellico, 1988).

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The splenic branches supply the spleen.

sections.title: References
sections.text:
Cortés, J. A. and Gómez Pellico, L. (1988) 'Arterial segmentation in the spleen', Surgical and Radiologic Anatomy, 10(4), pp. 323-332.

Pandey, S. K., Bhattacharya, S., Mishra, R. N. and Shukla, V. K. (2004) 'Anatomical variations of the splenic artery and its clinical implications', Clin Anat, 17(6), pp. 497-502.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Inferior phrenic artery.

Course: Inferiorly and or laterally towards the suprarenal gland.

Branches: Several small unnamed branches.

Supplied Structures: Suprarenal gland.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: Approximately four to five superior suprarenal arteries originate from the inferior phrenic artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text:
As each inferior phrenic artery courses upward towards the diaphragm, the superior suprarenal arteries emerge.

They travel directly towards the suprarenal gland, either in a lateral and or inferior direction according to their position in relation to the gland.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: Several small branches arise from each of the superior suprarenal arteries and anastomose with other suprarenal arteries prior to passing through the capsule of the suprarenal gland.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The superior suprarenal arteries supply the suprarenal gland.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Abdominal aorta.

Course: Superolaterally towards the suprarenal gland.

Branches: Small unnamed branches.

Supplied Structures: Suprarenal glands.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The middle suprarenal artery originates from the abdominal aorta with its contralateral counterpart at the lower border of the first lumbar vertebra (L1). This is at the same level as the superior mesenteric artery. It may also arise from the inferior phrenic or renal artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: On each side, the middle suprarenal arteries travel in a superolateral direction as they ascend over the lateral borders of the diaphragmatic crura. The right suprarenal artery travels posterior to the inferior vena cava. The arteries reach the inferomedial aspect of the suprarenal glands.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: Several small branches arise and anastomose with other suprarenal arteries prior to passing through the capsule of the suprarenal gland.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The middle suprarenal artery supplies the suprarenal gland.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Renal artery.

Course: Superiorly towards the suprarenal gland.

Branches: Small unnamed branches.

Supplied Structures: The suprarenal gland.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: One or two branches arise from the ipsilateral renal artery. Occasionally, the vessels may originate directly from the abdominal aorta or from the gonadal arteries.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The inferior suprarenal artery courses superolaterally and enters the inferior aspect of the adrenal gland.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: Several small branches arise and anastomose with other suprarenal arteries prior to passing through the capsule of the suprarenal gland.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The inferior suprarenal artery provides the main vascular supply to the suprarenal gland.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Common hepatic artery.

Course: Passes nearly vertically inferiorly, posterior to the first part of the duodenum.

Branches: Posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal, retroduodenal, supraduodenal, right gastroomental, and anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries.

Supplied Structures: Stomach, duodenum, pancreas, and greater omentum.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The gastroduodenal artery arises from the distal end of the common hepatic artery, posterior and superior to the first part of the duodenum.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The gastroduodenal artery descends inferiorly, posterior to the first (retroperitoneal) portion of the duodenum, to the left of the common bile duct.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The gastroduodenal artery gives rise to the posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal, retroduodenal, supraduodenal, right gastroomental, and anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The gastroduodenal artery supplies the stomach (right side, along greater curvature), and greater omentum (right side), duodenum (primarily its first and second parts), and pancreas (superior half).

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: External carotid artery.

Course: Travels posterosuperiorly, deep to the posterior belly of digastric muscle, passes between the mastoid process and transverse process of the atlas and passes in the occipital groove of the temporal bone. Finally, it ascends in the superficial fascia of the scalp.

Branches: Sternocleidomastoid, descending, auricular, and mastoid branches.

Supplied Structures: Muscles of the neck and scalp, meninges, pinna of the ear, and mastoid air cells.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The occipital artery arises from the posterior aspect of the external carotid artery. In some cases, it may arise as a common trunk with the posterior auricular artery in 14% of individuals as the occipitoauricular trunk (Tubbs et al, 2016).

sections.title: Course
sections.text:
At its origin, the occipital artery is crossed superficially by the hypoglossal nerve. It courses posteriorly and superiorly, deep to the posterior belly of the digastric muscle. It crosses the internal carotid artery and internal jugular vein, as well as the vagus and accessory nerves.

The occipital artery passes between the transverse process of the atlas (C1) and the mastoid process of the temporal bone. It then passes in the occipital groove of the temporal bone, medial to the mastoid process and the attachment sites of many muscles, including the sternocleidomastoid, splenius capitis, longissimus capitis, and digastric muscles. Here, it is joined by the greater occipital nerve. It pierces the investing layer of deep cervical fascia and ascends in the dense superficial fascia of the scalp in a tortuous fashion.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text:
The upper and lower sternocleidomastoid branches are considered the main branches of the occipital artery. The lower sternocleidomastoid branch arises close to the origin of the occipital artery, and in some cases, may arise directly from the external carotid artery. The upper sternocleidomastoid branch arises at the point where the occipital artery crosses the accessory nerve.

Additionally, between skin of the scalp and occipital belly of occipitofrontalis, the occipital artery divides into many branches, including descending, auricular, and mastoid branches. The terminal branches of the occipital artery anastomose with its fellow on the opposite side, as well as with the posterior auricular, superficial temporal arteries, transverse cervical branch of the subclavian artery.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The occipital artery supplies some muscles of the neck and scalp, including sternocleidomastoid, trapezius, and deep muscles of the neck. Additionally, it provides arterial branches to the meninges, pinna of the ear, and mastoid air cells.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Tubbs, R. S., Shoja, M. M. & Loukas, M. (2016) Bergman's Comprehensive Encyclopedia of Human Anatomic Variation. Wiley.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: External carotid artery.

Course: Ascends in the neck between the internal carotid artery and the pharynx.

Branches: Pharyngeal and Neuromeningeal trunks.

Supplied Structures: Pharynx, soft palate, ear, meninges.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The ascending pharyngeal artery is the smallest branch arising from the external carotid artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The ascending pharyngeal artery ascends from the medial surface of the external carotid artery, between the internal carotid artery and the pharynx, to the base of the cranium. The artery is crossed by the styloglossus and stylopharyngeus muscles.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The ascending pharyngeal artery gives rise to several pharyngeal branches and the Neuromeningeal trunk (Hacein-Bey et al, 2002). Additionally, it gives of several unnamed branches to the muscles and viscera of the neck.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The ascending pharyngeal artery supplies the pharynx, soft palate, the ear, and meninges. Additionally, as it ascends in the neck, it supplies branches to the longus capitis and longus colli muscles, the sympathetic trunk, the hypoglossal, glossopharyngeal, and vagus nerves, and some cervical lymph nodes.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Hacein-Bey, L., Daniels, D. L., Ulmer, J. L., Mark, L. P., Smith, M. M., Strottmann, J. M., Brown, D., Meyer, G. A. & Wackym, P. A. (2002) The Ascending Pharyngeal Artery: Branches, Anastomoses, and Clinical Significance. American Journal of Neuroradiology, 23(7), 1246.

21867.name: Pharyngeal Branches of Inferior Thyroid Artery

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Inferior thyroid artery.

Course: Travels medially towards lower part of pharynx.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Lower part of the pharynx.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The pharyngeal branches originate from the inferior thyroid artery as it ascends in the neck.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: From their origin the pharyngeal branches travel medially, posterior to the carotid sheath to reach the laryngopharynx.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The pharyngeal branches of the inferior thyroid artery supply the laryngopharynx, the lower part of the pharynx.

24009.name: Inferior Pharyngeal Branch of Pharyngeal Trunk

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Pharyngeal trunk.

Course: Medially towards the pharynx.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Inferior constrictor muscle of the pharynx.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The inferior pharyngeal branch of the pharyngeal trunk is a small irregular branch arising from the pharyngeal trunk as it ascends in the neck.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The inferior pharyngeal branch traverses medially towards the pharynx.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The inferior pharyngeal branch supplies inferior constrictor muscle of the pharynx.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Maxillary artery.

Course: Traverses the palatovaginal canal.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Mucosa of roof of nose, nasopharynx, sphenoid air sinus, and auditory tube.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The pharyngeal branch of the maxillary artery arises from the maxillary artery (Netter, 2011).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The pharyngeal branch of the maxillary artery enters the palatovaginal (pharyngeal) canal, a narrow canal in the roof of the nasal cavity.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The pharyngeal branch of the maxillary artery provides arterial supply to the mucosa of the roof of the nose, the nasopharynx, sphenoid air sinus, and the auditory tube (pharyngotympanic or Eustachian tube).

sections.title: References
sections.text: Netter, F. H. (2011) Atlas of Human Anatomy. Saunders/Elsevier.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Pharyngeal trunk.

Course: Medially towards the palatine tonsils.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Palatine tonsils.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The tonsillar branch of the pharyngeal trunk is a small irregular branch arising from the pharyngeal trunk as it ascends in the neck.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The tonsillar branch traverses medially towards the palatine tonsils.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The tonsillar branch supplies the palatine tonsils.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Ascending pharyngeal artery.

Course: Medially towards the pharynx.

Branches: Superior, middle, and inferior pharyngeal branches, Eustachian and tonsillar branches.

Supplied Structures: Constrictor muscles of the pharynx, auditory tube, and tonsils.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The pharyngeal trunk arises from the ascending pharyngeal artery as it ascends in the neck (Hacein-Bey et al, 2002).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The pharyngeal trunk traverses medially towards the pharynx.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The pharyngeal trunk gives rise to superior, middle, and inferior pharyngeal, Eustachian and tonsillar branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The pharyngeal trunk supplies the superior, middle, and inferior constrictor muscles of the pharynx and the stylopharyngeus muscle. A variable branch may descend between the superior constrictor and the levator veli palatini muscle to the soft palate, palatine tonsil, and auditory tube (Eustachian or pharyngotympanic tube).

sections.title: References
sections.text: Hacein-Bey, L., Daniels, D. L., Ulmer, J. L., Mark, L. P., Smith, M. M., Strottmann, J. M., Brown, D., Meyer, G. A. & Wackym, P. A. (2002) The Ascending Pharyngeal Artery: Branches, Anastomoses, and Clinical Significance. American Journal of Neuroradiology, 23(7), 1246.

18171.name: Tonsillar Branch of Dorsal Lingual Artery

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Dorsal lingual branches of lingual artery.

Course: Passes from the dorsum of the tongue towards the palatine tonsils.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Palatine tonsils.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The tonsillar branch arises from the dorsal lingual branch of the lingual artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The tonsillar branch of the dorsal lingual artery passes posteriorly from the dorsum of the tongue to the palatine tonsils.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The tonsillar branch of the dorsal lingual artery supplies the palatine tonsils.

18839.name: Middle Pharyngeal Branch of Pharyngeal Trunk

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Pharyngeal trunk.

Course: Medially towards the pharynx.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Middle constrictor muscle of the pharynx.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The middle pharyngeal branch of the pharyngeal trunk is a small irregular branch arising from the pharyngeal trunk as it ascends in the neck.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The middle pharyngeal branch traverses medially towards the pharynx.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The middle pharyngeal branch supplies the middle constrictor muscle of the pharynx.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Facial artery.

Course: Ascends between styloglossus and medial pterygoid muscles, pierces superior pharyngeal constrictor muscle to reach the palatine tonsils.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Palatine tonsils and superior pharyngeal constrictor muscle.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The tonsillar branch of the facial artery arises from the facial artery most commonly; however, it may arise from the ascending palatine artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The tonsillar branch of the facial artery ascends between the styloglossus and medial pterygoid muscles to reach the pharynx. At the superior border of the styloglossus muscle, the tonsillar branch pierces through the superior pharyngeal constrictor muscle to reach the inferior pole of the palatine tonsil.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The tonsillar branch of the facial artery provides the main blood supply to the palatine tonsils and superior pharyngeal constrictor muscle.

22110.name: Superior Pharyngeal Branch of Pharyngeal Trunk

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Pharyngeal trunk.

Course: Medially towards the pharynx.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Superior constrictor, levator veli palatini, and stylopharyngeus muscles.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The superior pharyngeal branch of the pharyngeal trunk is a small irregular branch arising from the pharyngeal trunk as it ascends in the neck.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The superior pharyngeal branch traverses medially towards the pharynx.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The superior pharyngeal branch supplies the superior constrictor, levator veli palatini, and stylopharyngeus muscles of the pharynx.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Maxillary artery.

Course: Passes from the pterygopalatine fossa to the oropharynx via the pterygoid canal.

Branches: Pharyngeal branch.

Supplied Structures: Pharynx, tympanic cavity, and auditory tube.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The artery of the pterygoid canal arises from the third part of the maxillary artery as it passes through the pterygopalatine fossa. Occasionally, the artery of the pterygoid canal arises from the internal carotid artery in the petrous part of the temporal bone (petrous part of the internal carotid artery).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: As its name suggests, the artery of the pterygoid canal passes through the pterygoid canal of the sphenoid bone, accompanied the nerve and vein of the pterygoid canal. The artery emerges from the canal in the oropharynx.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The artery of the pterygoid canal provides a pharyngeal branch in the oropharynx. Additionally, the artery of the pterygoid canal forms a complex anastomosis with the ethmoidal and sphenopalatine arteries in the pterygopalatine fossa. In the oropharynx, it anastomoses with the ascending pharyngeal, accessory meningeal, ascending palatine, and descending palatine arteries. Additionally, it anastomoses around the auditory tube (pharyngotympanic or Eustachian tube) (Standring, 2016).

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The artery of the pterygoid canal supplies the auditory tube, tympanic cavity, and upper pharynx.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Standring, S. (2016) Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. Gray's Anatomy Series 41 edn.: Elsevier Limited.

23499.name: Anterior Lateral Nasal Branches of Anterior Ethmoidal Artery
23499.latin: Rami nasales laterales anteriores arteriae ethmoideae anterioris

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Anterior ethmoidal artery.

Course: Descends into nasal cavity.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Lateral nasal wall.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The anterior lateral nasal branches of the anterior ethmoidal artery arise from the anterior ethmoidal artery as it passes through the anterior ethmoidal canal.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The anterior lateral nasal branches of the anterior ethmoidal artery descend into the nasal cavity.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: As the name suggests, the anterior lateral nasal branches of the anterior ethmoidal artery supply the lateral walls of the nasal cavity, including the anterior ethmoidal air cells and frontal sinus.

23167.name: Anterior Septal Branches of Anterior Ethmoidal Artery
23167.latin: Rami septales anteriores arteriae ethmoideae anterioris

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Anterior ethmoidal artery.

Course: Descends into nasal cavity.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Nasal septum.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The anterior septal branches of the anterior ethmoidal artery arise from the anterior ethmoidal artery as it passes through the anterior ethmoidal canal.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The anterior septal branches of the anterior ethmoidal artery descend into the nasal cavity, accompanied by the anterior ethmoidal nerve.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: As the name suggests, the anterior septal branches of the anterior ethmoidal artery supply the septum of the nasal cavity.

17041.name: Nasal Septal Branch of Superior Labial Artery
17041.latin: Ramus septi nasi arteriae labialis superioris

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Superior labial artery.

Course: Ascends and ramifies in the nasal septum.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Nose.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The nasal septal branch of superior labial artery arises from the superior labial artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The nasal septal branch ascends to the nasal septum.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: None.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The nasal septal branch of superior labial artery supplies the nasal septum.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Ophthalmic artery.

Course: Passes within the anterior ethmoidal canal and enters the anterior cranial fossa via the anterior ethmoidal foramen.

Branches: Anterior meningeal, anterior septal, and anterior lateral nasal branches.

Supplied Structures: Anterior ethmoidal cells, frontal sinus, dura mater, and nose.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The anterior ethmoidal artery arises from the ophthalmic artery as it passes anteromedially in the orbital cavity.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The anterior ethmoidal artery passes medially a short distance and enters the anterior ethmoidal canal. It then exits the canal into the anterior cranial fossa via the anterior ethmoidal foramen, just at the anterior end of the lateral edge of the cribriform plate.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The anterior ethmoidal artery has ramifications that arise both in the anterior ethmoidal canal (extracranially) and after it emerges from the anterior ethmoidal foramen (intracranially).

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The extracranial ramifications of the anterior ethmoidal artery supply the nasal cavity and septum, as well as the anterior ethmoidal cells and frontal sinus. The intracranial ramifications help supply the dura mater of the anterior cranial fossa.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Pamir, M. N., Black, P. M. L. & Fahlbusch, R. (2010) Meningiomas: A Comprehensive Text. Saunders/Elsevier.

19921.name: Septal Branches of Posterior Ethmoidal Artery

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Posterior ethmoidal artery.

Course: Descends into nasal cavity.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Nasal septum.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The septal branches of the posterior ethmoidal artery arise from the posterior ethmoidal artery as it passes through the posterior ethmoidal canal.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The septal branches of the posterior ethmoidal artery descend into the nasal cavity.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: As the name suggests, the septal branches of the posterior ethmoidal artery supply the septum of the nasal cavity.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Maxillary artery.

Course: Passes into nasal cavity.

Branches: Posterior lateral nasal artery and posterior septal branches.

Supplied Structures: Mucosa of nose and nasopharynx.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The sphenopalatine artery is a terminal branch of the third part of the maxillary artery as it passes through the pterygopalatine fossa.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The sphenopalatine artery passes into the nasal cavity through the sphenopalatine foramen, an opening between the pterygopalatine fossa and the nasal cavity.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The sphenopalatine artery divides into a posterior lateral nasal and posterior septal branches as it emerges through the sphenopalatine foramen.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The sphenopalatine artery is the main arterial contributor to the mucosa to the nose. Additionally, it supplies structures surrounding the nose and the nasopharynx.

20465.name: Posterior Lateral Nasal Branches of Sphenopalatine Artery
20465.latin: Rami nasales laterales posteriores arteriae sphenopalatinae

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Sphenopalatine artery.

Course: Pass anteriorly over the lateral wall of the nasal cavity.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Air sinuses and mucosa of the nasal cavity.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The posterior lateral nasal branches of the sphenopalatine artery arise from the sphenopalatine artery after it emerges in the nasal cavity through the sphenopalatine foramen.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The posterior lateral nasal branches of the sphenopalatine artery pass anteriorly, ramifying over the nasal conchae and meatuses of the nasal cavity.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches, however, the posterior lateral nasal branches of the sphenopalatine artery anastomose with the ethmoidal arteries and the nasal branches of the greater palatine artery.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The posterior lateral nasal branches of the sphenopalatine artery supply the mucosa of the lateral walls of the nasal cavity. Additionally, the posterior lateral nasal arteries supply the maxillary, ethmoidal, and sphenoidal air sinuses.

19326.name: Lateral Nasal Branches of Posterior Ethmoidal Artery
19326.latin: Rami nasales laterales arteriae ethmoideae posterioris

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Posterior ethmoidal artery.

Course: Descends into nasal cavity.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Lateral nasal wall.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The lateral nasal branches of the posterior ethmoidal artery arise from the posterior ethmoidal artery as it passes through the posterior ethmoidal canal.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The lateral nasal branches of the posterior ethmoidal artery descend into the nasal cavity.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: As the name suggests, the lateral nasal branches of the posterior ethmoidal artery supply the lateral walls of the nasal cavity, including the ethmoidal air cells.

22170.name: Posterior Septal Branches of Sphenopalatine Artery

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Sphenopalatine artery.

Course: Passes anteriorly along the nasal septum.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Mucosa of the nasal septum.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The posterior septal branches of the sphenopalatine artery arise from the sphenopalatine artery after it emerges in the nasal cavity through the sphenopalatine foramen.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The posterior septal branches of the sphenopalatine artery pass anteriorly on the nasal septum.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches, however, the posterior septal branches of the sphenopalatine artery anastomose with the ethmoidal arteries. Additionally, it anastomoses with the greater palatine artery that passes through the incisive canal.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The posterior septal branches of the sphenopalatine artery supply the mucosa of the nasal septum.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Ophthalmic artery.

Course: Passes within the posterior ethmoidal canal and enters the anterior cranial fossa via the posterior ethmoidal foramen.

Branches: Meningeal, septal, and lateral nasal branches.

Supplied Structures: Posterior ethmoidal cells, meninges, and nose.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The posterior ethmoidal artery arises from the ophthalmic artery as it passes anteromedially in the orbital cavity.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The posterior ethmoidal artery passes medially a short distance and enters the posterior ethmoidal canal. It then exits the canal into the anterior cranial fossa via the posterior ethmoidal foramen, just at the posterior end of the lateral edge of the cribriform plate.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The posterior ethmoidal artery has ramifications that arise both in the posterior ethmoidal canal (extracranially) and after it emerges from the posterior ethmoidal foramen (intracranially). Additionally, its intracranial ramifications may anastomose with meningeal branches of the internal carotid artery and with the middle meningeal artery (Pamir et al, 2010).

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The extracranial ramifications of the posterior ethmoidal artery supply the nasal cavity and septum, as well as the posterior ethmoidal cells. The intracranial ramifications help supply the dura mater of the medial third of the floor of the anterior cranial fossa (Pamir et al, 2010).

sections.title: References
sections.text: Pamir, M. N., Black, P. M. L. & Fahlbusch, R. (2010) Meningiomas: A Comprehensive Text. Saunders/Elsevier.

20045.name: Incisive Branch of Inferior Alveolar Artery

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Inferior alveolar artery.

Course: Courses medially in the mandible, below the incisor teeth.

Branches: Dental and peridental branches.

Supplied Structures: Mandibular dental arcade.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The incisive branch of the inferior alveolar artery is a continuation of the inferior alveolar artery once the mental artery arises.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The incisive branch of the inferior alveolar artery traverses the mandibular canal, accompanied by the terminal end of the inferior alveolar nerve.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The incisive branch of the inferior alveolar artery gives rise to dental and peridental branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The incisive branch of the inferior alveolar artery supplies the roots and pulp of the teeth of the lower jaw (i.e., the mandibular dental arcades).

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Infraorbital artery.

Course: Descends in lateral wall of maxillary sinus.

Branches: Dental and peridental branches.

Supplied Structures: Canine and lateral incisor teeth of maxillary dental arcade, maxillary sinus.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The middle superior alveolar arteries arise from the infraorbital artery as it passes through the infraorbital canal. This artery is not always present.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The middle superior alveolar arteries descend within the lateral wall of the maxillary sinus (Standring, 2016).

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The middle superior alveolar arteries divide into dental and peridental branches. They also form anastomoses with the anterior and posterior superior alveolar arteries.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The middle superior alveolar arteries supply the canine and lateral incisor teeth of the upper jaw. Additionally, it supplies the lateral aspect of the maxillary sinus.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Standring, S. (2016) Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. Gray's Anatomy Series 41 edn.: Elsevier Limited.

16645.name: Lingual Branch of Inferior Alveolar Artery

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Inferior Alveolar Artery.

Course: Descends with the lingual nerve.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Mucous membrane of the tongue.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The lingual branch of the inferior alveolar artery arises from the inferior alveolar artery near its origin.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The lingual branch of the inferior alveolar artery descends medial to the mandible, then passes under the mucosa of the mouth. It is accompanied by the lingual nerve.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The lingual branch of the inferior alveolar artery supplies the mucous membrane of the tongue.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Infraorbital artery.

Course: Descends in the lateral wall of maxillary sinus.

Branches: Dental and peridental branches.

Supplied Structures: Canine and incisor teeth of maxillary dental arcade, maxillary sinus.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The anterior superior alveolar arteries arise from the infraorbital artery as it passes through the infraorbital canal.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The anterior superior alveolar arteries descend within the anterior wall of the maxillary sinus.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The anterior superior alveolar artery divides into dental and peridental branches. Additionally, the anterior superior alveolar arteries form anastomoses with the posterior superior alveolar arteries, or the middle superior alveolar arteries when present.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The anterior superior alveolar arteries supply the incisor and canine teeth of the upper jaw.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Facial artery.

Course: Ascends between the styloglossus and stylopharyngeus muscles, then between the superior pharyngeal constrictor and medial pterygoid muscles.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Soft palate.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The ascending palatine artery arises from the facial artery, close to its origin from the external carotid artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: As its name suggests, the ascending palatine artery ascends between the styloglossus and stylopharyngeus muscles. As it reaches the pharynx, it continues to ascend between the superior pharyngeal constrictor and medial pterygoid muscles. Just below the levator veli palatine muscle, the ascending palatine artery gives off two terminal unnamed branches. One branch arches over the superior margin of the superior pharyngeal constrictor muscle to reach the soft palate, while another terminal branch pierces the superior pharyngeal constrictor muscle to reach the palatine tonsils and auditory tube.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The ascending palatine artery supplies the soft palate, tonsils, and auditory tube (Eustachian or pharyngotympanic tube).

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Lingual artery.

Course: Passes anteriorly on the ventral surface of the tongue.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Tongue.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The deep lingual artery is the terminal part of the lingual artery (the third part of the lingual artery) after the sublingual artery is given off.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: At the anterior border of the hyoglossus muscle, the deep lingual artery ascends between the genioglossus muscle medially and the inferior longitudinal muscle of the tongue laterally. It passes forwards in a tortuous manner near the lingual surface adjacent to the frenulum. Here it is accompanied by the lingual nerve.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The deep lingual artery supplies the tongue.

22134.name: Dorsal Lingual Branches of Lingual Artery

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Lingual artery.

Course: Ascend to the dorsum of the tongue.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Soft palate, tonsils, and adjacent areas.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The dorsal lingual branches of the lingual artery are the first branches arising from the lingual artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The dorsal lingual branches arise medial to the hyoglossus muscle. They ascend to the dorsum of the tongue.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The dorsal lingual branches give rise to a tonsillar branch. Additionally, it forms an anastomosis with its fellow branch from the opposite side.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The dorsal lingual branches of the lingual artery supply the soft palate, tonsils, epiglottis, palatoglossal arch, and adjacent mucous membrane.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: External carotid artery.

Course: Medially between the hyoglossus muscle and the middle constrictor muscle of the pharynx, then ascends between the genioglossus muscle and longitudinal muscle of the tongue.

Branches: Sublingual and deep lingual arteries, suprahyoid and dorsal lingual branches.

Supplied Structures: Tongue and floor of mouth.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The lingual artery arises from the anteromedial aspect of the external carotid artery. This occurs opposite the tip of the greater cornu of the hyoid bone, between the superior thyroid and facial arteries.

sections.title: Course
sections.text:
The lingual artery may be divided into thirds due to its relationship with the hyoglossus muscle. The first part of the lingual artery courses medially within the carotid triangle of the neck. It ascends slightly, then descends to the level of the hyoid bone, thus forming a loop that is crossed b the hypoglossal nerve.

The second part of the lingual artery courses along the superior border of the hyoid bone passing between the hyoglossus muscle and middle constrictor muscle of the pharynx. It crosses the ligament of the stylohyoid muscle and is accompanied by the lingual vein.

The third part of the lingual artery is called the deep lingual artery. At the anterior border of the hyoglossus muscle, it ascends between the genioglossus muscle medially and the inferior longitudinal muscle of the tongue laterally. It passes forwards near the lingual surface adjacent to the frenulum. Here it is accompanied by the lingual nerve.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The lingual artery has several named branches, including the dorsal lingual, sublingual, and deep lingual branches. Additionally, the branches of the lingual artery form a rich anastomosis to supply the musculature of the tongue.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The lingual artery provides the main arterial supply to the tongue and the floor of the mouth.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Maxillary artery.

Course: Descends in the greater palatine canal.

Branches: Greater and lesser palatine arteries.

Supplied Structures: Soft and hard palates.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The descending palatine artery is a terminal branch of the third part of the maxillary artery as it passes through the pterygopalatine fossa.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The descending palatine artery leaves the pterygopalatine fossa by descending in the greater palatine canal (pterygopalatine, palatomaxillary, or sphenopalatine canal), a canal in the sphenoid and palatine bones.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: The descending palatine artery terminates by giving rise to the greater and lesser palatine arteries before exiting the greater palatine canal.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The descending palatine artery supplies the hard and soft palates.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Maxillary artery.

Course: Descends slightly before entering the posterior superior alveolar foramina on the maxillary tuberosity.

Branches: Dental and peridental branches.

Supplied Structures: Molars and premolars of maxillary dental arcade, maxillary sinus.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The posterior superior alveolar artery arises from the maxillary artery as it passes through the pterygopalatine fossa (third part of the maxillary artery).

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The posterior superior alveolar artery descends slightly before entering the posterior superior alveolar foramina on the maxillary tuberosity.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: After passing through the posterior superior alveolar foramina, the posterior superior alveolar artery gives rise to dental and peridental branches, which penetrate the maxillary bone. Additionally, the posterior superior alveolar artery forms an anastomosis with the anterior superior alveolar artery (Fehrenbach & Herring, 2015).

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The branches of the posterior superior alveolar artery supply the maxillary sinus and the molars and premolars of the upper jaw.

sections.title: References
sections.text: Fehrenbach, M. J. & Herring, S. W. (2015) Illustrated Anatomy of the Head and Neck—E-Book. Elsevier Health Sciences.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Descending palatine artery.

Course: Passes anteriorly along the roof of the hard palate.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Hard palate, gingiva of maxillary teeth, nasal septum.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The greater palatine artery arises from the descending palatine artery in the greater palatine canal.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The greater palatine artery passes onto the hard palate through the greater palatine foramen of the bony palate and passes forwards on the hard palate.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches; however, the greater palatine artery continues into the incisive canal and forms an anastomosis with the sphenopalatine artery.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The greater palatine artery supplies the hard palate and the gingivae of the maxillary teeth. Additionally, through its anastomosis with the sphenopalatine artery, it helps supply the nasal septum.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Maxillary artery.

Course: Descends in the infratemporal fossa to enter mandibular foramen.

Branches: Mylohyoid, mental, dental, and peridental branches.

Supplied Structures: Lower jaw, lower lip, and chin.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The inferior alveolar artery arises from the maxillary artery. Sometimes, it may arise from a common trunk with the middle meningeal artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The inferior alveolar artery descends in the infratemporal fossa, posterior to the inferior alveolar nerve, lateral to the sphenomandibular ligament, and medial to the ramus of the mandible. It passes into the mandibular foramen on the mandible and traverses the mandibular canal, accompanied by the inferior alveolar nerve.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: Before entering the mandibular foramen, the inferior alveolar artery gives off a mylohyoid branch. Within the mandibular canal, it gives rise to mental, dental, and peridental branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The inferior alveolar artery supplies the lower jaw, lower lip, and chin.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Lingual artery.

Course: Passes anteriorly between the genioglossus and mylohyoid muscles.

Branches: No named branches.

Supplied Structures: Sublingual gland, mylohyoid muscle, and buccal and gingival mucous membranes.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The sublingual artery arises from the lingual artery, a branch of the external carotid artery.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The sublingual artery arises from the lingual artery at the anterior border of the hyoglossus muscle. It courses anteriorly between the genioglossus and mylohyoid muscles towards the sublingual gland.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches of the sublingual artery; however, it does contribute to several anastomoses. One branch pierces the mylohyoid muscle to join the submental branches of the facial artery. Another unnamed branch passes through the gingiva of the mandible to form an anastomosis with its fellow branch from the opposite side. From this anastomosis, a single artery arises and passes through the lingual foramen of the mandible.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The sublingual artery supplies the sublingual gland, the mylohyoid muscle, and the buccal and gingival mucous membranes.

sections.title: Quick Facts
sections.text:
Origin: Descending palatine artery.

Course: Passes posteriorly along the soft palate.

Branches: None.

Supplied Structures: Soft palate and palatine tonsils.

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: The lesser palatine artery arises from the descending palatine artery in the greater palatine canal.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: The lesser palatine artery passes onto the soft palate through the lesser palatine foramen of the palatine bone.

sections.title: Branches
sections.text: There are no named branches.

sections.title: Supplied Structures
sections.text: The lesser palatine artery supplies the soft palate and the tonsil.

23516.name: Posterior Glandular Branch of Superior Thyroid Artery
